description: SAS MERGE ... BY is a full outer join; reproduce it with the DataFrame method form and resolve overlapping columns explicitly.

sas_merge_by_is_outer_join.title: MERGE a b; BY key; is a full outer join on the BY variables -- use a.merge(b, on=keys, how='outer').
rule: SAS `MERGE a b; BY key;` is a **full outer join** on the BY variables, not an inner join.
Use the DataFrame **method** form `a.merge(b, on=keys, how="outer")`, not `pd.merge(a, b, ...)`. The left DataFrame drives the join and this reliably reproduces SAS behavior.
Both datasets must be sorted by the BY variables in SAS; pandas does not require sorting, but sort afterward if the SAS output order matters for QC.
If the same column exists in both (besides keys), SAS keeps the value from the **last** dataset listed. In pandas resolve suffixes explicitly and coalesce.
`IN=` dataset flags map to an indicator: `a.merge(b, on=keys, how="outer", indicator=True)` then filter on `_merge`.
pitfalls: Using pd.merge(a, b, ...) (function form) can diverge from SAS join semantics; prefer a.merge(b, ...).
Overlapping non-key columns: SAS keeps the LAST dataset's value, pandas makes _x/_y suffixes.

code: m = a.merge(b, on=keys, how="outer", indicator=True)   # IN= flags via _merge
both = m[m["_merge"] == "both"]                       # e.g. if a and b
